iterations.theme: Kusonje: potresna priča o pogibiji brata, šest mjeseci neizvjesnosti, ekshumaciji i borbi za istinu i pravdu

sections.subtitle: Dragovoljac koji se vratio iz Njemačke da bi branio Hrvatsku
sections.screenshot_description: Marijan priča kako se njegov brat, umjesto da ostane u Njemačkoj, prijavio u A satniju
sections.content:
Priča o Kusonjama u podcastu **Čušpajz** počinje odlukom jednog mladića. Marijan, gost epizode, govori o bratu koji je jedan dio vremena živio u Njemačkoj. Iako je ondje mogao ostati, takva mu misao, prema Marijanovim riječima, uopće nije pala na pamet. „Svi smo živjeli za taj dan“, prisjeća se Marijan atmosfere uoči rata. Brat se vratio, aktivirao i prijavio u **A satniju**.

Njihov posljednji susret dogodio se nakon što je iz bjelovarskog kraja stigla vijest o prvoj žrtvi. **Tihomir Vrdoljak** poginuo je 1. rujna u Doljanima. Brat je tada sa svojim prijateljem **Stipom Gadžom**, koji će kasnije poginuti zajedno s njim, svratio kući po neke stvari. Uz kratko „Idemo, idemo sad riješiti to“ obojica su otišla.

Marijan je tada imao 15 godina i, kako kaže, sve se odvijalo u smijehu. Nitko nije očekivao tragediju. Ide se negdje, ali na najgore se ne misli. Ističe da je danas teško sjetiti se kako je zapravo bilo, a da mladi to ne mogu ni shvatiti.

## Vrijeme bez mobitela

Gost podsjeća da tada nije bilo mobitela. Kućni telefoni bili su na takozvanim dvojnicima, odnosno dvostrukim brojevima. Netko je mogao biti u Daruvaru, udaljenom 30 do 40 kilometara, a obitelj nije imala pojma gdje se točno nalazi i što radi. Pakrac je od njihova doma bio udaljen oko 70 kilometara. Obitelj je kroz njega ponekad samo prolazila na putu prema Hercegovini, preko Okučana i Banje Luke.

Kad je trebalo ići braniti Hrvatsku, nije bilo spora ni kalkuliranja kamo se ide. „Oni su svi bili ekipa, dečki idu, odlaze“, sažima Marijan.
sections.subtitle_en: A volunteer who returned from Germany to defend Croatia
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marijan tells how his brother, instead of staying in Germany, enlisted in A Company
sections.content_en:
The story about Kusonje on the **Čušpajz** podcast begins with a decision made by a young man. Marijan, the guest of the episode, speaks about his brother who lived for a time in Germany. Although he could have stayed there, such a thought, according to Marijan's words, never even crossed his mind. „We all lived for that day“, Marijan recalls the atmosphere on the eve of the war. The brother returned, got involved, and enlisted in **A satnija**.

Their last meeting took place after the news arrived from the Bjelovar area about the first casualty. **Tihomir Vrdoljak** was killed on September 1 in Doljani. The brother then stopped by the house with his friend **Stipe Gadža**, who would later die together with him, to pick up some things. With a brief „Let's go, let's go handle that now“, both of them left.

Marijan was 15 years old at the time and, as he says, everything happened amidst laughter. No one expected a tragedy. You are going somewhere, but you don't think about the worst. He points out that today it is difficult to remember how it actually was, and that young people cannot even understand it.

## A time without mobile phones

The guest reminds that back then there were no mobile phones. Home telephones were on so-called party lines, that is, paired numbers. Someone could be in Daruvar, 30 to 40 kilometers away, and the family had no clue where exactly he was and what he was doing. Pakrac was about 70 kilometers away from their home. The family sometimes only passed through it on the way to Hercegovina, via Okučani and Banja Luka.

When it was necessary to go defend Croatia, there was neither dispute nor calculation as to where to go. „They were all a team, the guys are going, leaving“, Marijan summarizes.

sections.subtitle: A satnija 105. brigade: dečki koji su ostavili sve
sections.screenshot_description: Marijan objašnjava razliku između pravih dragovoljaca iz 1991. i kasnije mobiliziranih
sections.content:
Voditelj precizira da je riječ o A satniji. Marijan potvrđuje da se radi o **A satniji 105. bjelovarske brigade**.

Gost pritom uspoređuje i vlastito iskustvo. I sam je kasnije, 1995. godine, nekoliko dana sudjelovao u **Bljesku**. Kaže da je svaki dan proveden ondje bio težak, ali naglašava da se te okolnosti ne mogu mjeriti s 1991. godinom. Hrvatska vojska je 1995. bila organizirana i imala oružje. Dečki iz 1991. ostavljali su žene, djecu, poslove i normalan život te su sve išli žrtvovati za Hrvatsku.

Marijan vjeruje da nitko od bjelovarskih mladića prije toga nije bio ni u Pakracu. Ipak su otišli onamo braniti zemlju. „Nije se uopće razmišljalo jel ti hoćeš ili nećeš, nego ideš sa srcem“, ističe.

## Gorčina zbog izjednačavanja

Gosta posebno pogađa jedna nepravda. Status dragovoljca na kraju se izjednačio, pa ga danas imaju i oni koji su sjedili u uredu ili su se skrivali dok ih nisu mobilizirali. Ljudi poput njegova brata odlazili su sa svojim oružjem i u svojim uniformama. Na terenu su ga zatim mijenjali, pa je brat ondje zadužio pušku i oružje kojim je postrojba raspolagala.
sections.subtitle_en: A Company of the 105th Brigade: guys who left everything behind
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marijan explains the difference between real volunteers from 1991 and those mobilized later
sections.content_en:
The host clarifies that it is about A Company. Marijan confirms that it is about **A satnija 105. bjelovarske brigade**.

In doing so, the guest also compares his own experience. He himself later, in 1995, participated for several days in **Bljesak**. He says that every day spent there was difficult, but emphasizes that those circumstances cannot compare with the year 1991. In 1995, the Croatian Army was organized and had weapons. The guys from 1991 left their wives, children, jobs, and normal lives and went to sacrifice everything for Croatia.

Marijan believes that none of the young men from Bjelovar had ever even been to Pakrac before that. Still, they went there to defend the country. „There was no thinking at all about whether you want to or don't want to, but you go with your heart“, he points out.

## Bitterness because of equalization

One injustice particularly affects the guest. The volunteer status was ultimately equalized, so today it is held even by those who sat in an office or hid until they were mobilized. People like his brother left with their own weapons and in their own uniforms. They later exchanged them in the field, so the brother was issued a rifle and the weapons at the disposal of the unit there.

sections.subtitle: Oproštaj u šali i posljednji telefonski poziv
sections.screenshot_description: Marijan se prisjeća zadnjeg telefonskog razgovora večer prije akcije i šala na račun mame Jake
sections.content:
Voditelj pita sjeća li se Marijan dana odlaska, kad mu je brat rekao da ide „riješiti to“. Marijan se sjeća. Brat i Stipe Gadža došli su autom i izašli na petnaestak minuta. Bilo je to otprilike 2. rujna, po lijepom vremenu, dok su ljudi još izlazili na ulice. Oprostili su se na brzinu, gotovo u šali: tko sad ide nešto riješiti, „vidimo se“, i to je bilo sve.

Voditelj primjećuje da to govori koliko su ljudi tada imali srca i volje.

## „Jaka, ništa se ne boj“

Zadnji kontakt s obitelji bio je telefonski poziv iz Pakraca, večer prije akcije. Marijan je stajao pokraj telefona dok je razgovarala njegova pokojna majka. Dečki su se šalili, a većina ih je poznavala njegovu mamu **Jaku**, pa su je zezali: „Jaka, ništa se ne boj, mi smo tu svi.“ Ona im je dovikivala: „Daj, nemojte, pazite se.“

„I sve je bilo tako, ali eto, sutradan je…“, zastaje Marijan.

Voditelj napominje da je to bratu bio prvi teren. Marijan potvrđuje i dodaje da je nekolicina njegovih suboraca već ranije bila u Podravskoj Slatini. O tome zašto se i kako sve dogodilo može se, kaže, raspravljati sto puta, ali to su bila druga vremena. Noć prije akcije čuli su se posljednji put, a dečki su rekli samo: „Idemo tamo.“
sections.subtitle_en: A farewell in jest and the last telephone call
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marijan recalls the last telephone conversation the evening before the action and jokes at the expense of mom Jaka
sections.content_en:
The host asks whether Marijan remembers the day of departure, when his brother told him that he was going to „handle that“. Marijan remembers. The brother and Stipe Gadža came by car and stepped out for about fifteen minutes. It was approximately September 2, in nice weather, while people were still going out into the streets. They said goodbye quickly, almost in jest: who goes to handle something now, „see you“, and that was all.

The host observes that this speaks to how much heart and goodwill people had back then.

## „Jaka, don't be afraid of anything“

The last contact with the family was a telephone call from Pakrac, the evening before the action. Marijan stood next to the telephone while his late mother spoke. The guys were joking, and most of them knew his mom **Jaka**, so they teased her: „Jaka, don't be afraid of anything, we are all here.“ She called out to them: „Come on, don't, take care of yourselves.“

„And everything was like that, but well, the next day was…“, Marijan pauses.

The host notes that this was the brother's first deployment in the field. Marijan confirms and adds that several of his fellow combatants had already been to Podravska Slatina earlier. About why and how everything happened, one can, he says, debate a hundred times, but those were different times. The night before the action they heard from each other for the last time, and the guys only said: „We are going there.“

sections.subtitle: Nedjelja 8. rujna: vijest s Dnevnika
sections.screenshot_description: Marijan opisuje kako je kao petnaestogodišnjak na Dnevniku čuo vijest o stradanju bjelovarskih branitelja
sections.content:
Bila je nedjelja, 8. rujna. Petnaestogodišnji Marijan tada je trenirao nogomet i tog je dana išao na utakmicu. Kad se vratio kući, na **Dnevniku** je čuo da su bjelovarski branitelji kod Pakraca upali u nevolju.

Uslijedili su pokušaji da se nekoga dobije telefonom, uz misao koja se nameće u takvim trenucima: zašto baš oni, sigurno nije Stipe, sigurno nije brat. Ipak, Marijan priznaje da je njegov brat uvijek bio živ i spreman ići prvi. Kod njega nije bilo kalkuliranja.

## Istina privatnim kanalima

Tek navečer i sljedećeg dana, kad se dio ekipe vratio, potvrdilo se da su njegovi ondje „zaglavili“. Do 9. rujna obitelj je bila sigurna da je brat ostao na terenu.

Nitko iz vojske nije došao do obitelji niti joj je službeno izrazio sućut. Kako opisuje Marijan, sve je bilo prilično neorganizirano. Informacije su se dobivale privatnim kanalima, preko onih koje su poznavali. „I eto tako je počelo“, kaže Marijan. Idućih šest mjeseci danas opisuje kao „blagu katastrofu“ jer se, kaže, moralo živjeti šest mjeseci u neizvjesnosti.
sections.subtitle_en: Sunday, September 8: news from the Dnevnik
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marijan describes how as a fifteen-year-old he heard news on the Dnevnik about the suffering of the Bjelovar defenders
sections.content_en:
It was Sunday, September 8. The fifteen-year-old Marijan was training soccer at the time and went to a match that day. When he returned home, he heard on **Dnevnik** that the Bjelovar defenders near Pakrac had run into trouble.

Attempts to reach someone by telephone followed, along with the thought that imposes itself in such moments: why them of all people, surely it isn't Stipe, surely it isn't the brother. Still, Marijan admits that his brother was always alive and ready to go first. With him, there was no calculating.

## The truth through private channels

Only in the evening and the following day, when part of the crew returned, was it confirmed that his people had gotten „stuck“ there. By September 9, the family was certain that the brother had remained in the field.

No one from the army came to the family or officially expressed condolences to them. As Marijan describes, everything was quite disorganized. Information was obtained through private channels, through those they knew. „And well, that is how it started“, Marijan says. Today he describes the next six months as a „mild catastrophe“ because, he says, one had to live for six months in uncertainty.

sections.subtitle: Šest mjeseci glasina: od Titograda do noćnih poziva
sections.screenshot_description: Marijan priča o očevim pokušajima da preko poznanika iz JNA u Titogradu sazna je li brat zarobljen
sections.content:
Voditelj pita kako je obitelj živjela ne znajući ništa. Marijan objašnjava da im nitko nije došao reći istinu. Ljudi koji su bili na terenu možda su naslućivali da su njihovi suborci poginuli, ali nisu to mogli izgovoriti. Prvoga koji bi rekao da su „svi poginuli“ roditelji i rodbina bi, kaže gost, napali pitanjem: „Šta pričaš?“

Na voditeljevo pitanje jesu li se nadali da su dečki zarobljeni, Marijan opisuje vrijeme u kojem su kružile **tisuće priča**. Dolazili su ljudi, netko je predlagao da se pokuša nekoga nazvati, a nada se hranila svakom glasinom.

## Veza iz JNA

Posebno mjesto u sjećanju ima priča o ocu. Brat je vojni rok u JNA služio u **Titogradu**, u auto jedinici. Jednom je za velike kiše stajao u košulji. Ugledao ga je stariji čovjek i tako su se upoznali. Taj se čovjek zvao **Mišo**, bio je pukovnik i zapovjednik jedne titogradske vojarne.

Iz Hrvatske se tada više nije moglo dobiti Crnu Goru ni Srbiju, ali pokojni otac, koji je bio u Njemačkoj, uspijevao je dobiti Titograd. Preko te veze slao je čak i novac. Od nje su stizale priče da su dečki možda u Mitrovici, da je nekoliko njih ovdje, a nekoliko ondje. „Lakše ti je bilo vezati se u priču, jer još nije bilo tijela“, objašnjava Marijan.

## Disanje u slušalici

Obitelji su noću znali stizati anonimni pozivi. Podigla bi se slušalica, a s druge strane netko bi samo disao. Pozivatelja nije bilo moguće otkriti jer obitelj nije imala ni vlastiti broj, nego dvojnika.

Marijan je tada išao u srednju školu, ali kaže da zapravo nije ni bio u školi. Drugi brat bio je na fakultetu, a mama i tata u Njemačkoj.
sections.subtitle_en: Six months of rumors: from Titograd to late-night phone calls
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marijan speaks about his father's attempts to find out through an acquaintance from the JNA in Titograd whether his brother was captured
sections.content_en:
The host asks how the family lived knowing nothing. Marijan explains that no one came to tell them the truth. People who were in the field perhaps sensed that their fellow combatants had died, but they could not utter it. The first one who would say that „all of them died“, the parents and relatives would, says the guest, attack with the question: „What are you talking about?“

To the host's question whether they hoped that the guys were captured, Marijan describes a time in which **thousands of stories** circulated. People would come, someone would suggest trying to call someone, and hope was fed by every rumor.

## A contact from the JNA

A story about his father holds a special place in memory. The brother served his military service in the JNA in **Titograd**, in an automobile unit. Once, during heavy rain, he was standing in a shirt. An older man spotted him, and that is how they met. That man's name was **Mišo**, he was a colonel and commander of a Titograd barracks.

From Croatia at that time it was no longer possible to reach Montenegro or Serbia, but the late father, who was in Germany, managed to reach Titograd. Through that connection he even sent money. Stories arrived from it that the guys might be in Mitrovica, that a few of them were here, and a few there. „It was easier for you to tie yourself to a story, because there was no body yet“, Marijan explains.

## Breathing on the line

Anonymous calls used to reach the family at night. The receiver would be picked up, and on the other end someone would only breathe. It was not possible to discover the caller because the family did not even have their own number, but a party line.

Marijan was attending high school at the time, but says that he was actually not even at school. The other brother was at university, and mom and dad were in Germany.

sections.subtitle: Masovna grobnica, ekshumacija i sprovod 5. veljače 1992.
sections.screenshot_description: Marijan opisuje kako je brat identificiran prema osobnim stvarima nakon ekshumacije
sections.content:
Konačnu istinu obitelj je saznala tek ekshumacijom. Masovna grobnica otkrivena je 9. siječnja, kad je oslobođen dio područja oko **Buče** kod Pakraca. Ekshumacija je počela sredinom prvog mjeseca. Stradali su pokopani 5. veljače 1992. na **masovnom sprovodu**, šest mjeseci nakon pogibije.

Voditelj pita o dečkima koji su se probili iz okruženja. Marijan objašnjava da ni oni nisu mogli ništa sa sigurnošću tvrditi. Čuli su se stvari, a posljednji kontakti preko motorola bili su oko pola deset navečer. Ipak, nitko nije vidio što se dogodilo, pa nitko nije mogao pouzdano reći tko je poginuo. Čak i kad se za nekoga vjerovalo da je mrtav, ostajala je nada da je možda netko imao „malo ljudskosti“ i nekoga ostavio na životu.

## Identifikacija

Nada se ugasila ekshumacijom. Na identifikaciju je otišao Marijanov stariji brat, koji je vidio tijelo. Marijan nije išao, ali je vidio fotografije. Brat je identificiran prema osobnim stvarima.
sections.subtitle_en: Mass grave, exhumation, and funeral on February 5, 1992
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marijan describes how his brother was identified by personal belongings after the exhumation
sections.content_en:
The family learned the final truth only with the exhumation. The mass grave was discovered on January 9, when part of the area around **Buča** near Pakrac was liberated. The exhumation began in the middle of the first month. The victims were buried on February 5, 1992, at a **mass funeral**, six months after the deaths.

The host asks about the guys who broke through from the encirclement. Marijan explains that they too could not claim anything with certainty. Things were heard, and the last contacts via Motorola radios were around half past nine in the evening. Still, no one saw what happened, so no one could say reliably who had died. Even when someone was believed to be dead, there remained the hope that perhaps someone had „a little humanity“ and left someone alive.

## Identification

Hope was extinguished by the exhumation. Marijan's older brother went to the identification, and he saw the body. Marijan did not go, but he saw the photographs. The brother was identified by personal belongings.

sections.subtitle: Vrećice u Ministarstvu: osobne stvari nakon 33 godine
sections.screenshot_description: Marijan priča o sastanku u Ministarstvu branitelja na kojem su obitelji dobile osobne stvari stradalih
sections.content:
Mjesec dana prije snimanja Marijan je s drugima bio na sastanku kod **Medveda** u **Ministarstvu branitelja**. Na ulasku su primijetili da gospodin Medved nosi neke vrećice. U njima su bile **osobne stvari stradalih branitelja**, vraćene obiteljima 33 godine nakon ekshumacije.

Put tih stvari do obitelji Marijan opisuje kao puki slučaj. Ležale su bačene u jednoj sobi **Zavoda za sudsku medicinu** u Zagrebu. Pronađene su tek kad se nakon **potresa** uređivao prostor. Netko je tada nazvao Ministarstvo, a ondje su reagirali i povezali stvari s obiteljima.

Marijan je osobno dobio jedan privjesak. Takve su privjeske nosili svi pripadnici A satnije kako bi se međusobno raspoznavali. Kad ga je primio, nije ni znao što je to, pa je pitao suborce, koji su mu potvrdili. Među vraćenim stvarima bili su i:
- satovi,
- lančići,
- druge osnovne osobne stvari.

„Kad netko kaže, prošlo je… nama te rane nikad ne mogu proći“, kaže Marijan. Voditelj dodaje da se te rane mogu samo ponovno otvoriti.

## Spomen na Hrvoja

Voditelj priznaje da ne zna što bi rekao. Spominje **Hrvoja**, s kojim se čuo početkom ljeta i koji mu je u kasnom telefonskom razgovoru ispričao mnogo toga. Ističe da „bez njega ne može“, a Marijan potvrđuje da Hrvoja nema. Voditelj kaže da na ovakvu priču čovjek nema normalan komentar i da se čini kao da se sudbina poigrava s obiteljima.
sections.subtitle_en: Bags at the Ministry: personal belongings after 33 years
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marijan talks about a meeting at the Ministry of Croatian Veterans where families received the personal belongings of the deceased
sections.content_en:
A month before the recording, Marijan was with others at a meeting with **Medved** at the **Ministarstvo branitelja**. Upon entering, they noticed that Mr. Medved was carrying some bags. Inside them were the **personal belongings of the fallen defenders**, returned to the families 33 years after the exhumation.

Marijan describes the journey of those items to the families as mere chance. They were lying discarded in a room of the **Zavod za sudsku medicinu** in Zagreb. They were found only when the space was being renovated after the **earthquake**. Someone then called the Ministry, and there they reacted and connected the items with the families.

Marijan personally received a pendant. Such pendants were worn by all members of A Company in order to recognize each other. When he received it, he didn't even know what it was, so he asked fellow combatants, who confirmed it for him. Among the returned items were also:
- watches,
- small chains,
- other basic personal belongings.

„When someone says, it has passed… for us those wounds can never heal“, Marijan says. The host adds that those wounds can only open up again.

## Remembrance of Hrvoje

The host admits that he does not know what to say. He mentions **Hrvoje**, with whom he was in touch at the beginning of summer and who told him many things during a late-night telephone conversation. He points out that „without him one cannot“, and Marijan confirms that Hrvoje is gone. The host says that about such a story a person has no normal comment and that it seems as if fate is playing games with the families.

sections.subtitle: Zahvalnost i ljutnja: roditelji koji nisu dočekali
sections.screenshot_description: Marijan govori o pomiješanim osjećajima i roditeljima koji su umrli prije povrata stvari
sections.content:
Marijan opisuje dvojake osjećaje. S jedne strane drago mu je i zahvalan je. Naglašava da nema ništa protiv Ministarstva branitelja i odaje mu priznanje što je reagiralo. Dobiti nešto što je pripadalo bratu, kaže, neizrecivo mu znači.

S druge strane ljut je zbog odnosa prema tim stvarima, koje su tolike godine mogle ležati bačene bez ikakve brige.

Najteže mu pada vrijeme koje je u međuvremenu prošlo. Njegovi otac i majka umrli su prošle godine i nisu dočekali povrat stvari. Isto se dogodilo i većini drugih obitelji, a kod nekih više nema nikoga živog tko bi ih primio.

„Usred svega toga što se izdogađalo, pa smo se nekako i navikli, sve je to više i normalno, prihvaćaš, ali eto, daleko je to od normalnog“, zaključuje Marijan.
sections.subtitle_en: Gratitude and anger: parents who did not live to see it
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marijan talks about mixed feelings and parents who died before the return of the belongings
sections.content_en:
Marijan describes twofold feelings. On the one hand, he is glad and grateful. He emphasizes that he has nothing against the Ministry of Croatian Veterans and gives it credit for reacting. Receiving something that belonged to his brother, he says, means indescribably much to him.

On the other hand, he is angry because of the attitude toward those items, which could lie discarded for so many years without any care.

What hits him the hardest is the time that has passed in the meantime. His father and mother died last year and did not live to see the return of the belongings. The same happened to most of the other families, and with some, there is no one alive left to receive them.

„In the midst of all that has happened, so we kind of got used to it, all that is even normal anymore, you accept it, but well, that is far from normal“, Marijan concludes.

sections.subtitle: Koliko ih je stradalo? Borba udruge protiv dezinformacija
sections.screenshot_description: Voditelj i Marijan razgovaraju o različitim brojkama stradalih branitelja
sections.content:
Nakon šest mjeseci iščekivanja uslijedila je još jedna potresna spoznaja. Kad se išlo vidjeti što se dogodilo, pokazalo se da je dio dečki ubijen odmah, u kući.

Voditelj se zatim osvrće na **cilj udruge** i prenosi Hrvojeve riječi da je oko ovog slučaja puno laži i dezinformacija. Za početak se ne zna ni točan broj stradalih. U medijima se navodi 17 branitelja, a neki govore o 20.

Marijan to razjašnjava ovako:
- **18** je broj koji uključuje **Tadiju Markića**. On se vodi pod tim imenom, ali je neidentificiran i nitko ga nije priznao.
- Uz njih su bila i dvojica branitelja koji su došli iz Zagreba pomoći, **Ivantić** i **Mato Čančar**.
- Ukupno je ondje, prema Marijanu, bilo **20** ljudi.

Voditelj dodaje da mu je Hrvoje u telefonskom razgovoru rekao kako je ekshumacijom pronađeno 17 tijela i još troje civila.
sections.subtitle_en: How many died? The association's fight against disinformation
sections.screenshot_description_en: The host and Marijan discuss different numbers of fallen defenders
sections.content_en:
After six months of anticipation, another harrowing realization followed. When they went to see what happened, it turned out that part of the guys were killed immediately, in the house.

The host then turns to the **goal of the association** and conveys Hrvoje's words that there are many lies and disinformation surrounding this case. To begin with, not even the exact number of victims is known. In the media, 17 defenders are stated, and some speak of 20.

Marijan clarifies it like this:
- **18** is the number that includes **Tadija Markić**. He is listed under that name, but is unidentified and no one has recognized him.
- Along with them were two defenders who came from Zagreb to help, **Ivantić** and **Mato Čančar**.
- In total there were, according to Marijan, **20** people there.

The host adds that Hrvoje told him in a phone conversation that 17 bodies and three more civilians were found during the exhumation.

sections.subtitle: „Neki neće spavati mirno“: poruka da će se pravda izvršiti
sections.screenshot_description: Marijan poručuje da udruga neće odustati dok odgovorni za zločin ne odgovaraju
sections.content:
Na voditeljevo pitanje otkriva li udruga sada pravu istinu, Marijan odgovara da se s dolaskom mlađih članova i većim angažmanom tek sada vide mnoge stvari. Kritičan je prema državi. Ističe da kao da nitko nije imao volje posvetiti se ovom slučaju, uključujući i službe kojima bi to trebao biti posao.

## Osuđeni na slobodi, drugi bez optužnice

Gost opisuje sudski epilog:
- **Četvorica** su osuđena. Nakon odsluženih otprilike dvije trećine kazne, na temelju sporazuma otišli su u **Srbiju**, a neki od njih i danas su živi.
- Ostala je **masa ljudi** povezanih sa zločinom protiv kojih odvjetništvo i sudstvo nikada nisu podigli nikakvu optužnicu.

Voditelj napominje da neki od njih navodno i danas žive u tom kraju. Marijan je oprezan i ne želi upirati prstom, ali poruka mu je jasna. Neki, kaže, „neće spavati mirno“. Dok su živi članovi udruge, kojoj se sada priključuju i mlađi ljudi, pobrinut će se da se kad-tad pravda izvrši i da odgovorni plate za ono što su učinili.
sections.subtitle_en: „Some will not sleep peacefully“: a message that justice will be served
sections.screenshot_description_en: Marijan conveys that the association will not give up until those responsible for the crime are held accountable
sections.content_en:
To the host's question whether the association is now discovering the real truth, Marijan replies that with the arrival of younger members and greater engagement, many things are only now being seen. He is critical of the state. He points out that it was as if no one had the will to dedicate themselves to this case, including the services whose job that was supposed to be.

## Convicted persons at liberty, others without indictment

The guest describes the judicial outcome:
- **Four** were convicted. After serving approximately two-thirds of the sentence, on the basis of an agreement they went to **Srbija**, and some of them are still alive today.
- There remained a **mass of people** connected with the crime against whom the state attorney's office and judiciary never brought any indictment.

The host notes that some of them allegedly still live in that region today. Marijan is cautious and does not want to point fingers, but his message is clear. Some, he says, „will not sleep peacefully“. As long as the members of the association are alive, joined now by younger people, they will make sure that sooner or later justice is served and that those responsible pay for what they did.
